methodology.name: ACTED
methodology.headline: Five dimensions. Better evidence.
methodology.intro: ACTED helps interviewers assess what candidates have actually done — through 35 clearly defined competencies and 350 curated behavioural questions.

dimensions.name: Adapt
good: Shows honest reflection and clear personal learning.
Adapts behaviour in response to evidence.
watchOuts: Gives a polished answer without genuine reflection.
Cannot explain what changed as a result.

dimensions.name: Connect
good: Builds trust and understands different perspectives.
watchOuts: Relies on authority rather than influence.
Cannot separate personal contribution from the team’s work.

dimensions.name: Think
good: Connects decisions to wider context and consequences.
watchOuts: Leaps to conclusions or relies on assertion.
Cannot explain the reasoning behind the decision.

dimensions.name: Enable
good: Creates clarity, ownership and space for others to succeed.
Tailors support to individual and team needs.
Links people decisions to measurable outcomes.
watchOuts: Takes over rather than enabling others.
Avoids accountability or difficult performance issues.

dimensions.name: Deliver
good: Takes clear ownership and follows through.
Prioritises resources against the intended outcome.
watchOuts: Waits for direction when action is needed.

competencies.name: Self-Awareness
competencies.definition: Understands personal strengths, limitations, impact and triggers and uses that insight to improve effectiveness.

questions.text: Tell me about feedback you received that surprised you. What did you do with it?
Give me an example of when you recognised the effect your behaviour was having on others. How did you notice, and what did you change?
Describe a limitation of yours that you have had to work around. How do you manage it?
Tell me about a time one of your strengths worked against you. What did you notice?
Give me an example of a situation or person that reliably provokes a strong reaction in you. How do you handle that?
Tell me about a working relationship that was difficult partly because of something in your own approach. What did you do?
Looking back, describe a change in your own behaviour that you deliberately made. What prompted it, and how have you sustained it?
Tell me about a blind spot you did not see until someone pointed it out. How did you respond?
Describe how your leadership or working style has changed over time. What drove the change?
Tell me about a time your view of yourself differed sharply from how others saw you. How did you make sense of that?

competencies.name: Continuous Growth
competencies.definition: Actively seeks feedback, reflection and development experiences and converts learning into sustained changes in behaviour or capability.

questions.text: Tell me about something you have deliberately worked on developing recently. Why that, and how have you gone about it?
Give me an example of when you sought out feedback rather than waiting for it. What did you ask, and what did you do with the answer?
Describe a capability you had to build because your role demanded it. How did you learn it?
Tell me about a stretch experience you sought out for yourself. What did you gain from it?
Give me an example of feedback that was hard to hear. How did you respond at the time, and afterwards?
Tell me about a development goal you set but did not achieve. What got in the way?
Looking back, describe a habit you have changed. What made the change stick?
Tell me about the most significant learning you have taken from a failure. How has it changed what you do?
Describe a pattern you have noticed in the feedback you receive. What have you done about it?
Tell me about a time you had to develop a capability that did not come naturally to you. How did you approach it?

competencies.name: Learns & Adapts
competencies.definition: Learns quickly from experience and evidence and adjusts assumptions, behaviour or approach when circumstances change.

questions.text: Tell me about a time you had to get up to speed quickly in an unfamiliar area. How did you do it?
Give me an example of when you changed your approach because it was not working. What did you notice?
Describe a time new information made you rethink something you had already decided. What did you do?
Tell me about a time you had to unlearn a way of working that had served you well before. What made that necessary?
Give me an example of when you applied something you learned in one setting to a very different one. How did you adapt it?
Tell me about a time your environment changed significantly — a new role, new leadership or a new market. How did you adjust?
Looking back, describe a time you were slow to adapt. What did that cost, and what finally alerted you?
Tell me about the steepest learning curve you have faced. How did you manage it, and what was the result?
Describe a time you changed a strongly held view in the face of new evidence. What convinced you?
Tell me about a time you had to lead others through something new while still learning it yourself. How did you handle it?

competencies.name: Navigates Ambiguity
competencies.definition: Remains effective when information, direction or outcomes are unclear and progresses work without requiring false certainty.

questions.text: Tell me about a time you had to make progress without clear direction. What did you do?
Give me an example of when you had to start something with no precedent or template to follow. How did you begin?
Describe a time you had to act before all the information was available. How did you decide when to move?
Tell me about a time the goalposts kept moving. How did you keep the work going?
Give me an example of when responsibility or ownership was genuinely unclear. How did you handle it?
Tell me about a time you had to keep a team working productively through prolonged uncertainty. What did you do?
Looking back, describe a time you pressed for certainty that was not available. What did that cost you?
Tell me about the most ambiguous situation you have had to lead through. How did you approach it?
Describe a time the same information could reasonably be read several different ways. How did you choose a course of action?
Tell me about a decision you made under real uncertainty that you still believe was right, whatever the outcome. Why?

competencies.name: Resilience
competencies.definition: Sustains effectiveness through pressure, setbacks and prolonged challenge while recovering constructively and maintaining perspective.

questions.text: Tell me about a significant setback you experienced at work. How did you deal with it?
Give me an example of when you had to keep performing under sustained pressure. What helped you?
Describe a time something you had worked hard on did not succeed. How did you respond?
Tell me about a prolonged difficult period at work. How did you sustain your effectiveness through it?
Give me an example of when you had to absorb criticism or a decision that went against you. How did you handle it?
Tell me about a time you had to manage several heavy demands at once. How did you keep perspective?
Looking back, describe a time pressure affected you more than you would have liked. What did you learn about your limits?
Tell me about the most demanding professional period you have been through. How did you recover from it?
Describe a time you had to support others through pressure while under considerable pressure yourself. How did you manage both?
Tell me about a professional disappointment, such as a role you did not get or a decision that went against you. How did you handle it, and what did you do next?

competencies.name: Situational Adaptability
competencies.definition: Reads changing people and circumstances accurately and flexes style, pace or approach without losing sight of the required outcome.

questions.text: Tell me about a time you changed your approach for a particular person or audience. What did you read in the situation?
Give me an example of when conditions changed part-way through something. How did you adjust?
Describe a time you had to work at a different pace from the one you would normally choose. How did you handle it?
Tell me about a time your usual style was not working with someone. What did you change?
Give me an example of when you got an unexpected reaction from someone. How did you respond in the moment?
Tell me about a time you joined a team or organisation with a very different culture from what you were used to. How did you adapt?
Looking back, describe a time you adapted so much that you lost sight of the outcome you needed. What did you learn?
Tell me about the most demanding situation where you had to change approach quickly under pressure. What did you do?
Describe a time different people in the same situation needed very different things from you. How did you manage that?
Tell me about a time you had to judge whether to adapt or hold your ground. How did you decide?

competencies.name: Courage & Authenticity
competencies.definition: Acts consistently with values, raises difficult issues and expresses a considered point of view even when doing so carries personal or professional risk.

questions.text: Tell me about a time you raised an issue that others preferred not to discuss. What made you decide it needed to be said?
Tell me about a time when speaking up did not produce the outcome you wanted. What did you learn about courage and judgement from the experience?
Describe a situation where doing what you believed was right carried a meaningful personal or professional risk. What did you do?
Tell me about a time you disagreed openly with someone significantly more senior than you. How did you handle the disagreement, and what happened?
Give me an example of when organisational pressure conflicted with your own judgement or values. How did you respond?
Describe a situation where you had to deliver a message you knew would be unpopular. How did you balance candour with the impact on others?
Describe a situation where remaining silent would have been easier. Why did you choose to act, and would you make the same choice again?
Tell me about a time you changed your position publicly after realising you were wrong. What enabled you to do that?
Tell me about a time you chose not to compromise on an important principle. What were the consequences?
Give me an example of when you exposed a weakness, mistake or uncertainty of your own rather than protecting your image. What happened?

competencies.name: Communicates with Impact
competencies.definition: Conveys ideas clearly and credibly, adapts messages to the audience and creates understanding, engagement and action.

questions.text: Tell me about a time you had to explain something complex simply. How did you approach it?
Give me an example of when you adapted your message for a particular audience. What did you change?
Describe a time you had to deliver a difficult message. How did you prepare, and how did it land?
Tell me about a time you had to make your case to a senior audience with very little time. How did you structure what you said?
Give me an example of when something you wrote — a paper, proposal or report — changed a decision. What made it effective?
Tell me about a time you realised you were not being understood. What did you do?
Looking back, describe a communication of yours that went badly. What would you do differently?
Tell me about the highest-stakes presentation or discussion you have led. How did you prepare, and what was the outcome?
Describe a time you had to communicate bad news or significant uncertainty to a large group. How did you handle it?
Tell me about a time you had to listen carefully before you could communicate effectively. What did you hear that changed your approach?

competencies.name: Builds Relationships & Networks
competencies.definition: Creates and sustains trusted relationships and networks that enable information, influence, support and organisational effectiveness.

questions.text: Tell me about a working relationship you built that proved valuable. How did you establish it?
Give me an example of when you got something done through people who did not report to you. How did the relationships help?
Describe how you built relationships when you started in a new role or team. What did you do first?
Tell me about a time you invested in a relationship before you needed anything from it. How did that pay off?
Give me an example of when your network gave you information or insight you would not otherwise have had. What did you do with it?
Tell me about a difficult stakeholder or colleague you had to build a relationship with. How did you approach them?
Looking back, describe a relationship you neglected or handled badly. What did you learn from it?
Tell me about the most important external relationship or partnership you have built. What did it achieve?
Describe a time you deliberately built connections across the organisation to make something possible. How did you go about it?
Tell me about a time an important relationship broke down. What did you do to rebuild it, and how did it end up?

competencies.name: Works Collaboratively
competencies.definition: Builds productive partnerships across boundaries, shares ownership and enables others to contribute to shared outcomes.

questions.text: Tell me about a time you worked with another team or function to achieve something neither could have done alone. What was your contribution?
Give me an example of when you supported another team with no direct benefit to your own objectives. What prompted you?
Describe a time you had to build a working relationship with a team you had not worked with before. How did you go about it?
Tell me about a time your objectives and another team's pulled in different directions. How did you find a way forward?
Give me an example of when you depended on someone outside your control to deliver. How did you manage that?
Tell me about a time collaboration was not working well. What did you do to change it?
Looking back, describe a joint piece of work that did not succeed. What was your part in that, and what would you do differently?
Tell me about the most complex piece of cross-organisational work you have been involved in. How did you keep people working together?
Describe a time you put the wider organisational outcome ahead of your own team's interests. What did it cost, and how did you handle it?
Tell me about a time there was tension over ownership, credit or territory between teams. How did you deal with it?

competencies.name: Navigates Conflict
competencies.definition: Surfaces and addresses disagreement constructively, balancing candour, relationships and the need to reach workable resolution.

questions.text: Tell me about a disagreement you had with a colleague. How did you resolve it?
Give me an example of when you raised a difficult issue with someone rather than letting it continue. How did the conversation go?
Describe a time you had to find a workable resolution between two people or groups who disagreed. What did you do?
Tell me about a disagreement that had been allowed to run on unaddressed. How did you tackle it?
Give me an example of when emotions were running high in a discussion. How did you keep it constructive?
Tell me about a time you disagreed with a decision but had to work with it. How did you handle that?
Looking back, describe a conflict you handled poorly. What would you do differently now?
Tell me about the most difficult conflict you have had to resolve. What made it hard, and what was the outcome?
Describe a disagreement involving people significantly more senior than you. How did you handle it?
Tell me about a working relationship that had broken down and needed repairing. What did you do?

competencies.name: Influences Others
competencies.definition: Shapes decisions and behaviour through credibility, evidence, relationships and an approach tailored to the people and context involved.

questions.text: Tell me about a time you changed someone's mind. What was your argument, and why did it work?
Give me an example of when you had to influence someone over whom you had no authority. How did you go about it?
Describe a time you used evidence to persuade someone. How did you present it?
Tell me about a time you had to influence someone who was resistant from the outset. What approach did you take?
Give me an example of when you tailored your case to different people's interests. What did you change for each of them?
Tell me about a time you built support from several people before making a proposal. How did you do it?
Looking back, describe a time you failed to influence an outcome you cared about. What would you do differently?
Tell me about the most significant decision you have influenced. What did you do to shift it?
Describe a time you had to move a senior group towards a position they did not initially favour. How did you manage it?
Tell me about a time you had to negotiate an outcome between parties with genuinely conflicting interests. How did you reach agreement?

competencies.name: Stakeholder Leadership
competencies.definition: Builds alignment among stakeholders with different needs, manages expectations and sustains commitment to important outcomes.

questions.text: Tell me about a time you had to manage stakeholders with different expectations. How did you handle it?
Give me an example of when you had to reset a stakeholder's expectations. How did you approach the conversation?
Describe a time you built alignment among people who initially wanted different things. What did you do?
Tell me about a time a senior stakeholder wanted something you did not think was right. How did you handle it?
Give me an example of when you had to keep stakeholders committed over a long piece of work. What did you do?
Tell me about a time you had to tell a stakeholder something they did not want to hear. How did you manage it?
Looking back, describe a stakeholder relationship you would manage differently now. What went wrong?
Tell me about the most difficult set of stakeholders you have had to align. What made it hard, and what was the outcome?
Describe a time you had to recover a stakeholder relationship after a failure or a broken commitment. What did you do?
Tell me about a time you had to hold a position against sustained stakeholder pressure. How did you handle it?

competencies.name: Organisational Awareness
competencies.definition: Reads organisational dynamics, informal networks, competing interests and context and uses that understanding constructively.

questions.text: Tell me about a time you needed to understand how decisions were really made in an organisation. How did you work it out?
Give me an example of when knowing the right people helped you get something done. How did you use that?
Describe a time you identified someone whose support was essential but who was not obviously involved. What did you do?
Tell me about a time you had to navigate competing agendas to move something forward. How did you handle it?
Give me an example of when you adjusted your approach because of the sensitivities involved. What did you take into account?
Tell me about a time you misread the organisational context. What happened, and what did you learn?
Looking back, describe a time an aspect of the culture made progress difficult. Did you work with it or around it, and why?
Tell me about the most politically complex situation you have navigated. How did you handle it, and what was the result?
Describe a time you built support quietly before raising something formally. How did you go about it?
Tell me about a time you had to decide whether to challenge a power dynamic or work within it. How did you judge that?

competencies.name: Critical Thinking & Judgement
competencies.definition: Evaluates complex or incomplete information objectively, tests assumptions and reaches well-reasoned decisions.

questions.text: Tell me about a complex problem you had to work through. How did you break it down, and what conclusion did you reach?
Give me an example of when you tested an assumption that others were treating as fact. What prompted you, and what did you find?
Describe a time you faced conflicting evidence or advice. How did you decide what to believe?
Tell me about a decision where the quick answer and the right answer were different. How did you handle the pressure to move fast?
Give me an example of when you got to the root cause of a recurring problem rather than treating the symptom. How did you get there?
Tell me about a time you had to take people who disagreed with you through your reasoning. How did you approach it?
Looking back, describe a conclusion you reached that proved wrong. What in your reasoning would you change?
Tell me about the most difficult judgement call you have made with significant consequences. What made it hard, and what was the outcome?
Describe a time you had to act on information you knew was incomplete or unreliable. How did you manage the risk of being wrong?
Tell me about a time you changed your position on an important decision after someone challenged your reasoning. What convinced you?

competencies.name: Strategic Perspective
competencies.definition: Sees beyond immediate priorities, identifies emerging opportunities and risks, and connects decisions to longer-term organisational goals.

questions.text: Tell me about a decision you made with the longer term in mind rather than the immediate result. What was the trade-off?
Give me an example of when you saw an opportunity or risk emerging before others did. What did you notice, and what did you do about it?
Describe a time you connected your team's day-to-day work to a broader organisational goal. How did you make that link real for people?
Tell me about a time you accepted weaker short-term performance to protect a longer-term objective. How did you justify that?
Give me an example of when an external trend — regulatory, technological, economic or social — changed your plans. How did you respond?
Tell me about a time you had to persuade others to look beyond immediate pressures. What argument worked?
Looking back, describe a strategic decision you were involved in that did not deliver what was expected. What did it teach you about your own judgement?
Tell me about the most significant change of direction you have shaped or led. What convinced you it was necessary?
Describe a time you had to plan for a future you could not predict with any confidence. How did you approach it?
Tell me about a time your view of the longer-term direction differed from that of senior colleagues. How did you handle it?

competencies.name: Business & Commercial Acumen
competencies.definition: Understands how the organisation creates value and uses commercial, financial and market insight to make sound business decisions.

questions.text: Tell me about a decision you made where the commercial implications mattered. What evidence did you rely on, and what did you decide?
Give me an example of when you improved revenue, margin or cost in a way that could be measured. What did you personally contribute, and how do you know it worked?
Describe a time a shift in your market, sector or funding environment affected your work. How did you spot it, and what did you change?
Tell me about a time you had to choose between the financially attractive option and the one that was better for the organisation in other ways. How did you weigh it up?
Give me an example of when you questioned a business case, forecast or set of numbers that others had accepted. What did you challenge, and what happened?
Tell me about a time you had to make a commercial or financial argument to people who did not naturally think in those terms. How did you get it to land?
Looking back, describe a commercial decision you would take differently now. What did the outcome teach you about how you assess value?
Tell me about the most significant investment, bid or spending decision you have shaped. How did you build your recommendation, and what was the result?
Describe a time you had to reach a commercial judgement when the data was incomplete or the assumptions were contested. How did you move forward?
Tell me about a time a competitor, new entrant or external change threatened part of your business. What did you propose, and how did it play out?

competencies.name: Customer Orientation
competencies.definition: Builds a deep understanding of customer needs and translates it into decisions, priorities and solutions that create lasting value.

questions.text: Tell me about a time you identified a customer need that was not being met. How did you find it, and what did you do about it?
Give me an example of when you changed a product, service or process because of what customers told you. What difference did it make?
Describe a situation where a customer asked for one thing but you judged they needed something different. How did you handle it?
Tell me about a time you had to balance what a customer wanted against cost, risk or what the organisation could realistically deliver. What did you decide?
Give me an example of when your first attempt to solve a customer problem did not work. What did you notice, and what did you do next?
Tell me about a time you had to persuade colleagues to prioritise a customer issue they saw as less important. How did you make the case?
Looking back, describe a customer relationship you would manage differently now. What changed your thinking?
Tell me about the most serious service failure or complaint you have dealt with. What did you do, and what happened to the relationship afterwards?
Describe a time customer feedback was mixed or contradictory and you still had to act. How did you decide whose needs came first?
Tell me about a time you argued for a decision that was right for customers but unpopular internally. How did you handle the resistance?

competencies.name: Digital Fluency
competencies.definition: Understands the possibilities and implications of digital technology and data, and uses them to improve decisions, experiences and performance.

questions.text: Tell me about a time you used data to inform a decision. What did the data show, and what did you do?
Give me an example of when you introduced or adopted a new technology or digital tool. What difference did it make?
Describe a time you identified a manual or repetitive process that technology could improve. What did you do about it?
Tell me about a time you had to learn an unfamiliar system or technology quickly. How did you go about it?
Give me an example of when a technology or data project did not deliver what was expected. What went wrong, and how did you respond?
Tell me about a time you had to bring people with you who were uncomfortable with a new system or way of working. How did you do it?
Looking back, describe a time you had to weigh the benefits of a digital solution against its cost, risk or impact on people. What did you decide?
Tell me about the most significant digital or data-driven change you have led or contributed to. What was the impact?
Describe a time you had to make a decision when the available data was poor, incomplete or contradictory. How did you handle it?
Tell me about a time you had to weigh the risks of a technology — security, privacy, ethics or over-reliance — against its benefits. What did you conclude?

competencies.name: Global Mindset
competencies.definition: Considers different markets, cultures and perspectives and adapts decisions to succeed across geographic and cultural boundaries.

questions.text: Tell me about a time you worked with colleagues, customers or partners from a different country or culture. What did you do differently as a result?
Give me an example of when you adapted a product, service or way of working for a different market or location. What did you change, and why?
Describe a time you realised an assumption you held did not apply in another market or culture. How did you find out, and what did you do?
Tell me about a time you had to balance a global or organisation-wide standard against genuine local needs. How did you resolve it?
Give me an example of when a cultural difference caused a misunderstanding in your work. How did you address it, and what changed afterwards?
Tell me about a time you had to build agreement across teams in different countries or time zones. What made it difficult, and how did you manage it?
Looking back, describe a decision involving another market or culture that you would approach differently now. What did you learn?
Tell me about the most complex piece of work you have led across multiple countries or cultures. What made it challenging, and what was the outcome?
Describe a time you had to make a decision affecting a market you did not know well. How did you inform your judgement?
Tell me about a time local practice or expectation conflicted with an organisational policy or standard. How did you handle it?

competencies.name: Drives Innovation
competencies.definition: Challenges established thinking, generates useful new ideas and turns promising concepts into practical improvements.

questions.text: Tell me about an idea of yours that changed how something was done. Where did the idea come from, and what happened to it?
Give me an example of when you challenged the way things had always been done. What did you propose, and how was it received?
Describe a time you found a workable solution with very limited time, budget or resource. What did you do?
Tell me about an idea you tested on a small scale before committing to it. What did the trial tell you, and what did you do next?
Give me an example of an idea of yours that did not work. How did you decide whether to stop, change or persist?
Tell me about a time you had to win support for an unproven idea. How did you handle the scepticism?
Looking back, describe an innovation you would introduce differently now. What would you change about how you developed or launched it?
Tell me about the most significant new approach you have taken from idea through to full implementation. What made it difficult?
Describe a time you had to judge whether a promising idea was worth the risk or disruption it would cause. How did you decide?
Tell me about a time you had to scale something that worked well in one area into a much wider setting. What did you have to change?

competencies.name: Creates Vision & Purpose
competencies.definition: Articulates a compelling future direction, connects it to organisational purpose and helps others understand their role in achieving it.

questions.text: Tell me about a time you set out a clear direction for a team or piece of work. How did you describe it?
Give me an example of when you helped someone understand how their work contributed to something bigger. What did you say?
Describe a time you had to give people a sense of purpose during routine or difficult work. What did you do?
Tell me about a time you had to translate an organisational strategy into something meaningful for your team. How did you do it?
Give me an example of when you had to change or refresh a direction people had already committed to. How did you handle it?
Tell me about a time people did not connect with the direction you set. What did you do about it?
Looking back, describe an ambition you set that proved unrealistic. What did you learn?
Tell me about the most ambitious direction you have set and mobilised people behind. What was the outcome?
Describe a time you had to articulate a direction when the future was genuinely uncertain. How did you handle that honestly?
Tell me about a time you had to sustain belief in a long-term direction when short-term results were poor. What did you do?

competencies.name: Builds Trust
competencies.definition: Earns confidence through integrity, consistency, openness, sound judgement and reliable follow-through.

questions.text: Tell me about a time someone trusted you with something significant. What had you done to earn that?
Give me an example of when you told someone an uncomfortable truth. How did you handle it?
Describe a time you made a commitment that proved difficult to keep. What did you do?
Tell me about a time you made a mistake that affected others. How did you handle it?
Give me an example of when you were open about your reasoning for a decision people disagreed with. What effect did that have?
Tell me about a time you had to handle sensitive or confidential information. How did you manage the competing pressures?
Looking back, describe a time you did something that damaged others' confidence in you. What did you learn?
Tell me about a relationship or team where trust had been lost. What did you do to rebuild it?
Describe a time you were under pressure to say or do something you did not believe was right. How did you respond?
Tell me about a time being consistent was difficult because different people expected different things from you. How did you handle it?

competencies.name: Attracts Talent
competencies.definition: Identifies the capabilities required for future success and attracts, assesses and selects strong and diverse talent against those needs.

questions.text: Tell me about a time you had to determine what kind of talent a team would need for its next stage, rather than simply replacing someone who had left.
Give me an example of when you had to balance speed of hiring against quality of hire. How did you manage the trade-off?
Describe a difficult hiring decision where two credible candidates offered very different strengths. How did you assess what the organisation really needed?
Tell me about a time you successfully attracted someone who was not actively looking to move. What made your opportunity compelling to them?
Give me an example of when you challenged an established hiring profile or selection criterion. What prompted you to question it, and what happened?
Tell me about a hiring decision you got wrong. What did you miss during assessment, and how has it changed the way you assess talent?
Tell me about the strongest person you have hired or helped select. What did you recognise in them that others might have overlooked?
Describe a time when you deliberately broadened a candidate pool. What did you change, and how did it affect the quality or diversity of the shortlist?
Describe a time when a candidate looked excellent on paper but you had reservations. What evidence did you seek, and what decision did you make?
Tell me about a role where current capability was not enough to define the hire. How did you assess candidates for future potential as well as immediate fit?

competencies.name: Develops People
competencies.definition: Builds others' capability through purposeful feedback, coaching, challenge, opportunity and development experiences.

questions.text: Tell me about someone you helped develop. What did you do, and what changed for them?
Give me an example of development feedback you gave that was difficult but useful. How did you handle it?
Describe a time you identified a development need in someone. How did you raise it, and what did you put in place?
Tell me about a time you gave someone a stretching opportunity. How did you support them, and how did it go?
Give me an example of when you coached someone through a problem rather than solving it for them. What approach did you take?
Tell me about a time you worked with someone who was underperforming. What did you do, and what was the outcome?
Looking back, describe a time your attempt to develop someone did not work. What would you do differently?
Tell me about the most significant change you have seen in someone as a result of your investment in them. What did you do?
Describe a time you developed someone for a role beyond your own team, knowing you might lose them. How did you approach it?
Tell me about a time you gave honest development feedback to someone who did not accept it. How did you handle that?

competencies.name: Values Diversity
competencies.definition: Actively seeks, respects and uses different backgrounds, experiences and perspectives to improve decisions and outcomes.

questions.text: Tell me about a time working with people whose backgrounds or perspectives differed from yours improved the outcome. What did you do to make use of those differences?
Give me an example of when you sought out a perspective that was missing from a discussion. What prompted you, and what difference did it make?
Describe a time you noticed someone was not being heard or included. What did you do?
Tell me about a time you changed your own view after hearing a perspective very different from your own. What shifted your thinking?
Give me an example of when you challenged an assumption, comment or practice that excluded people. How did you handle it?
Tell me about a time you had to work closely with someone whose style or outlook you found difficult. How did you build a productive relationship?
Looking back, describe a time you recognised bias in a decision, process or shortlist. What did you do about it?
Tell me about the most meaningful thing you have done to make a team or process more inclusive. What changed as a result?
Describe a time you supported a minority or dissenting view in a group that was moving towards consensus. What happened?
Tell me about a barrier to inclusion you identified in how work was designed or decisions were made. What did you do about it?

competencies.name: Builds High-Performing Teams
competencies.definition: Creates the conditions for teams to combine clear purpose, complementary strengths, trust and disciplined execution.

questions.text: Tell me about a team you helped build or strengthen. What did you do, and how did its performance change?
Give me an example of how you established clear purpose and roles in a team. What difference did it make?
Describe a time you brought together people with different strengths to achieve something. How did you make the mix work?
Tell me about a time trust was lacking in a team you led or were part of. What did you do?
Give me an example of when you set or reset how a team worked together — its standards, rhythms or ways of operating. What prompted it?
Tell me about a time a team you led was not performing well. How did you diagnose the problem, and what did you change?
Looking back, describe a team decision or intervention you would handle differently now. What did you learn?
Tell me about the highest-performing team you have led or been part of. What specifically created that performance?
Describe a time you had to sustain a team's performance through significant change, loss or pressure. What did you do?
Tell me about a time you addressed behaviour that was undermining a team, even though the individual was a strong performer. What did you do?

competencies.name: Inspires Engagement
competencies.definition: Connects people to meaningful goals, understands what motivates them and creates conditions in which they choose to contribute their best.

questions.text: Tell me about a time you motivated a person or team to give more than the minimum. What did you do?
Give me an example of when you connected people's work to something they found meaningful. How did you do it?
Describe a time you noticed morale was low. What did you do about it?
Tell me about a time you had to keep people engaged through a difficult or uncertain period. What worked?
Give me an example of when you learned what motivated an individual and adjusted your approach accordingly. What difference did it make?
Tell me about a time you gave people genuine ownership of something. How did you decide how much to let go of?
Looking back, describe a time your attempt to lift engagement did not work. What did you learn?
Tell me about the most disengaged team or individual you have worked with. What did you do, and what changed?
Describe a time you had to build commitment to a change people did not want or were tired of. How did you approach it?
Tell me about a time you had to sustain motivation over a long period with few visible wins. How did you do it?

competencies.name: Provides Direction
competencies.definition: Creates clarity about priorities, expectations and outcomes so others know what matters and how to move forward.

questions.text: Tell me about a time you gave a team or individual clarity about what mattered most. How did you do it?
Give me an example of when you set objectives or expectations for others. How did you make sure they were understood?
Describe a situation where people were unclear about who was doing what. How did you resolve it?
Tell me about a time you had to change direction and re-explain priorities to your team. How did you handle the disruption?
Give me an example of when you delegated a significant piece of work. How did you set it up, and how closely did you stay involved?
Tell me about a time you had to turn a broad or complex objective into practical work for others. How did you approach it?
Looking back, describe a time your direction was misunderstood or not followed. What did it teach you about how you set expectations?
Tell me about the most difficult message about priorities or performance expectations you have had to give a team. How did you deliver it?
Describe a time you had to give people direction when you did not yet have clear answers yourself. What did you tell them?
Tell me about a time you had to create clarity across teams that did not report to you. How did you do it?

competencies.name: Plans & Prioritises
competencies.definition: Translates objectives into practical plans, sequences work effectively and adjusts priorities as circumstances change.

questions.text: Tell me about a piece of work with several moving parts that you had to plan. How did you structure it?
Give me an example of when you had more to do than the time allowed. How did you decide what came first?
Describe a time you worked to a demanding deadline. How did you plan the work to meet it?
Tell me about a time you had to reprioritise significantly part-way through. What triggered it, and how did you manage the change?
Give me an example of a plan that depended on other teams or external parties. How did you manage those dependencies?
Tell me about a time different stakeholders wanted different things done first. How did you settle the order of priority?
Looking back, describe a plan of yours that did not survive contact with reality. What did it teach you about how you plan?
Tell me about the most complex project or programme you have planned. How did you keep it on track?
Describe a time an unexpected disruption forced you to rebuild your plan at short notice. What did you do?
Tell me about a time you stopped or postponed something to protect a more important priority. How did you make that case?

competencies.name: Takes Action
competencies.definition: Moves from intent to action with appropriate pace, initiative and ownership, particularly when circumstances are difficult or uncertain.

questions.text: Tell me about a time you acted on a problem that was not formally yours to solve. What prompted you, and what did you do?
Give me an example of when you had to act quickly with little time to consult. How did you decide what to do?
Describe a situation where something was going wrong and everyone was waiting for someone else to move. What did you do?
Tell me about a time you removed an obstacle that was holding up progress. How did you tackle it?
Give me an example of when you acted decisively and it turned out to be the wrong call. What did you do next?
Tell me about a time you pushed ahead without full agreement or complete information. How did you manage the risk?
Looking back, describe a time you held off acting and later wished you had moved sooner. What held you back?
Tell me about the most demanding situation where you had to take charge at short notice. What did you do first, and how did it turn out?
Describe a time you took personal ownership of a difficult problem others were avoiding. What happened?
Tell me about a time you had to balance urgency against the risk of acting too soon. How did you judge the right moment?

competencies.name: Uses Resources Effectively
competencies.definition: Deploys people, time, money and other resources thoughtfully to maximise impact and minimise waste.

questions.text: Tell me about a time you delivered something worthwhile with fewer resources than you would have wanted. How did you make it work?
Give me an example of when you identified waste, duplication or unnecessary cost. What did you change?
Describe a time you had to allocate limited people, time or budget across competing demands. How did you decide?
Tell me about a time you moved resources away from one activity to strengthen another. How did you justify it?
Give me an example of when your team or project was beyond its capacity. What did you do about it?
Tell me about a time an unexpected demand arrived with no additional resource. How did you absorb it?
Looking back, describe a resourcing decision you would make differently now. What did the outcome teach you?
Tell me about the most difficult resourcing trade-off you have had to make. Who was affected, and how did you handle it?
Describe a time you needed scarce expertise or capability you did not control. How did you secure it?
Tell me about a time you had to challenge or defend a resource decision with senior colleagues. What was the outcome?

competencies.name: Improves Ways of Working
competencies.definition: Identifies opportunities to simplify, strengthen or redesign processes and converts them into sustainable improvements.

questions.text: Tell me about a process you improved. What was wrong with it, and what did you change?
Give me an example of when you simplified something that had become unnecessarily complicated. What was the effect?
Describe a time you noticed a recurring problem in how work was being done. What did you do about it?
Tell me about an improvement that required people to change their habits. How did you get it adopted?
Give me an example of when you met resistance to a change in working practice. How did you handle it?
Tell me about a time you had to establish whether an improvement had actually worked. What did you measure, and what did it show?
Looking back, describe an improvement that did not stick. Why do you think that was, and what would you do differently?
Tell me about the most significant redesign of a process or way of working you have led. What made it difficult?
Describe a time you improved a process that crossed several teams or functions. How did you get agreement?
Tell me about a time you had to choose between standardising an approach and allowing local flexibility. How did you judge it?

competencies.name: Creates Accountability
competencies.definition: Sets clear commitments and standards, monitors progress and follows through constructively when expectations are not met.

questions.text: Tell me about a time you set clear commitments or standards for a piece of work. How did you make them stick?
Give me an example of when someone did not deliver what they had committed to. How did you handle it?
Describe a situation where ownership of a task was unclear. What did you do?
Tell me about a time you held someone to account without damaging the working relationship. How did you approach the conversation?
Give me an example of how you tracked progress on something important. What did you do when it began to slip?
Tell me about a time you had to hold a peer or someone more senior to a commitment. How did you handle it?
Looking back, describe a time you did not follow up as firmly as you should have. What was the consequence?
Tell me about the most difficult accountability conversation you have had. What made it hard, and what was the outcome?
Describe a time you took responsibility for a mistake or failure in your area. What did you do?
Tell me about a time you had to build accountability in a group where no one had authority over the others. How did you do it?

competencies.name: Delivers Results
competencies.definition: Maintains focus on meaningful outcomes, overcomes obstacles and consistently converts commitments into measurable results.

questions.text: Tell me about a demanding target or outcome you achieved. What did you personally do to get there?
Give me an example of when you overcame a significant obstacle to deliver something. What did you do?
Describe a time you delivered under real time pressure. How did you protect the quality of the work?
Tell me about a time a result you were responsible for was at risk. How did you spot it, and what did you do?
Give me an example of when you had to deliver while managing several competing demands. How did you keep focus?
Tell me about a time you turned around an underperforming piece of work, team or account. What did you change?
Looking back, describe a time you fell short of a commitment. What did you do about it, and what has it changed in how you work?
Tell me about the most significant result you have delivered. What was your contribution, and how was the impact measured?
Describe a time you had to sustain performance over a long or difficult period. How did you keep it going?
Tell me about a time you had to judge whether to keep pushing for a result or accept it was not achievable. How did you decide?

ratingScale.label: Significantly Below Requirement
ratingScale.meaning: Little or no relevant evidence, or evidence raising material concerns.

ratingScale.label: Below Requirement
ratingScale.meaning: Limited or inconsistent evidence; meaningful gaps are apparent.

ratingScale.label: Meets Requirement
ratingScale.meaning: Clear and sufficient evidence that the required capability is present.

ratingScale.label: Above Requirement
ratingScale.meaning: Strong, relevant evidence above the expected level.

ratingScale.label: Significantly Above Requirement
ratingScale.meaning: Consistent, compelling evidence significantly above the level required.

howToUse: Each interviewer covers the competencies allocated to them. Interviewers alternate asking questions.
Ask the primary question first. Use the backup only if a second angle is needed or the candidate struggles to provide sufficient evidence.
Probe for a specific past example and the candidate’s personal contribution.
Capture notes during the interview. Score each competency afterwards, then discuss and agree final ratings as a panel.

star.label: Task
star.pack: What challenge did the candidate face and what was their responsibility?
star.live: What was the candidate responsible for?

star.label: Action
star.pack: What specific actions did the candidate personally take?

star.label: Result
star.pack: What happened, how was it measured and what did they learn?
star.live: What changed, and what did they learn?

guidance.evaluation: Record individual observations, then agree the final score as a panel. The panel—not a numerical average—makes the hiring decision.
guidance.competencyStep: Select the capabilities that are genuinely critical to success in the role.
guidance.coverageAdvice: We recommend at least one competency from each dimension.
guidance.coverageComplete: A broad evidence base for this interview.
guidance.questionStep: Choose two different questions for every selected competency.
guidance.panelHelp: Questions rotate between interviewers in this order. Add up to five.
